heading: WEST JAVA PROVINCE
HAS DECIDED:
translated_text:
HAS DECIDED:

To Establish REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN.

heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

General

heading: Article 1
translated_text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. City Region hereinafter referred to as Region is the Bandung City Region.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bandung.
4. Regional Government Administration is the implementation of government affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy in the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Institution which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
6. Woman is a person or human being who has a womb, experiences menstruation, pregnancy, gives birth to children and breastfeeds.
7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, cultural resources, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention.
9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children, or father and children or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upwards and downwards up to the third degree.
10. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of government affairs which are the authority of the Region.
11. Every Person is an individual or corporation, whether a legal entity or not a legal entity.
12. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women.
13. Service is an activity and immediate action carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Handling is an action taken to provide complaint services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement, legal services, repatriation, and social reintegration.
15. Assistant is a trusted person who has the competence to accompany Victims in accessing the right to handling, protection and recovery.
16. Assistance is an activity and action carried out by an assistant during the service process.
17. Institution is an Office/Agency/Office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
19. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of Integrated Services for women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
20. Integrated Service is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for Victims, Victims' Families, and/or Witnesses of Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence.

PROTECTIONOFWOMEN

Part One

General

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

1. Every Woman victim of violence has the right to obtain protection and continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.
2. Handling of Women victims of violence must be kept confidential unless otherwise determined by the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. In the event of violence, every victim has the right to obtain professional Assistance services based on the victim's condition and needs.
4. The Regional Government provides integrated Services for comprehensive and integrated protection and handling.
5. Integrated services as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Women's Empowerment and child protection affairs.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Forms of Violence Against Women

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

1. Forms of Violence against Women include:
a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence;
c. economic violence; and
d. psychological violence.
2. Forms of physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, include any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
3. Forms of sexual violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, include sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forcing intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or other non-commercial purposes.
4. Forms of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, include neglect of Women by not providing a decent living.
5. Forms of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d include acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to the victim.

Article 17 (1) Every Woman victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) Protection of Women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to Women who experience violence in the family environment, the Community, the education sector, offices and the business sector.

heading: Part Three
Part Four
Part Five
CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 27 (1) The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision over Women's Empowerment and Protection.

2. The form of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of monitoring and evaluation activities over Women's Empowerment and Protection.

19-

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 28 (1) The Community may participate in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection policies.

2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), may be submitted through the submission of suggestions, opinions orally and in writing through the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
3. The Community, community institutions/organizations and the business world individually and/or institutionally may participate in the financing/funding of Women's Empowerment and Protection programs and activities organized by the Regional Government.
4. The Community, community institutions/organizations and the business world individually and/or institutionally may participate in monitoring and evaluation.
5. Every form of Community participation is recorded and reported to the Regional Government through the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
6. The Regional Government may give awards to the Community that has played an active role and has met the requirements in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

FINANCING

Article 29 Financing for the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection activities, may be sourced from: a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and b. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 30 This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone knows, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation with its placement in the Regional Gazette of the City of Bandung.

Enacted in Bandung on the date of 30 June 2025 MAYOR OF BANDUNG, signed.

heading: ELUCIDATION
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF THE CITY OF BANDUNG

NUMBER 7 OF 2025

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HR) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unequal treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals and between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women that makes women vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.

Women have equal rights with men, however in certain discriminatory conditions, the government is obliged to implement affirmative action so that the rights of women and women in vulnerable groups need to receive protection so as not to experience violence and can live a decent life according to the principles of humanity, equality and justice. Women's empowerment and women's protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To carry out these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data.
22- The Bandung City Government as the party that has the authority to regulate and protect the citizens of Bandung City, deems it necessary to continuously carry out and formulate regulations to provide guarantees for women's empowerment and women's protection in Bandung City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various development sectors, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.
